name: Matrix, Arctic and Tropical Interpretations of a Duplicating Rule
description: Rules out tracked matrix, arctic and tropical orientations under pumps and unboundedness. No fixed-row, row-sum or lexicographic matrix measure globally orients KO7.

program.name: The Termination Axis
program.summary: The rule recΔ b s (δ n) → app s (recΔ b s n) copies its payload and consumes one counter; a direct measure orients it exactly when it ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter, and the additive, affine, matrix, arctic, tropical and Knuth-Bendix families fail under their stated premises, with mutual cycles and higher-order sharing as variants. The proofs that succeed change the observer: the dependency-pair projection to the counter, nonlinear coupling, and the lexicographic and multiset path orders; seventy-six methods and a residual catalog record the verdicts as bookkeeping.

oneLine: No pumped or unbounded tracked, fixed-row, row-sum, lexicographic, arctic-primary or tropical matrix measure globally orients KO7, while tropical root orientation never lifts to wrapper contexts.
summary: The theory studies matrix, arctic and tropical interpretations of a duplicating recursor rule and whether any such measure can orient all KO7 steps. Objects include fixed-dimension componentwise measures, arbitrary mixed matrices with scalarization witnesses, natural matrices with wrapper-diagonal positivity, max-plus measures, and arctic and tropical carriers with finite-part projections. The question is whether tracked, fixed-row, row-sum or lexicographic orders can decrease along the duplicating wrap-versus-recur step and hence globally orient the system. Main results say they cannot under unbounded range, successor-pump or wrapper-pump hypotheses, and natural strict orders are blocked by wrapper-diagonal positivity alone with one positive value needed for nonincreasing orders. Certificate-backed arctic and tropical barriers add matching weight and scalarization certificates plus unbounded scalarized range, while tropical root orientation exists yet never extends to the full wrapper-context closure. A one-dimensional tropical escape witness and the Boolean monotone interpretation show the certificate-free tropical and lift claims fail without certificates.
boundary: On one side, pumped or unbounded interpretations cannot orient the duplicating step: wrapper gain dominates the pumped branch, so strict tracked decrease would force a strict natural increase already ruled out by the scalar barrier. The obstruction is the duplicating wrap-versus-recur step together with unbounded range, successor drift of at least one, wrapper drift of at least one, or positive wrapper diagonals. On the other side, bounded behavior, zero or bot diagonals, and one-sided wrapper policies escape: a bot-right arctic measure and a tropical escape measure orient root steps, while full wrapper-context closure remains impossible for every tropical measure.

conclusions.statement: For every dimension d, every measure M over ko7Schema, every order R, every dominance witness D linking M.weight to R, and every unbounded scalarized range witness, M.eval with R does not globally orient ko7System.

Given dimension d, measure M over ko7Schema, coordinate i, wrapper-diagonal positivity for M at i, and order R implying u i < v i whenever R u v holds, M.eval with R does not globally orient ko7System.

Given dimension d, measure M over ko7Schema, coordinate i with wrapper-diagonal positivity, order R implying u i <= v i whenever R u v holds, and a term t with 1 <= M.eval t i, M.eval with R does not globally orient ko7System.
Given measure M over ko7Schema with unbounded first-component range, M.eval with PairLt does not globally orient ko7System.
Given dimension d, tracked coordinate, measure M over ko7Schema, and unbounded tracked range, M.eval with VecLt does not globally orient ko7System.
Given dimension d and measure M over ko7Schema carrying its own primary pump, M.eval with VecLexLt does not globally orient ko7System.
Given dimension d and measure M over ko7Schema carrying its own primary pump, M.eval with VecPermLexLt at M.priority does not globally orient ko7System.
Given KO7 max measure M with unbounded range, M.eval with less-than does not globally orient ko7System.
Given arctic primary measure M over ko7Schema and unbounded max range of its projectedMax, M.eval with ArcticLt does not globally orient ko7System.
For every type beta, given tropical primary measure M over ko7Schema with unbounded max range of its projectedMax, M.eval with M.lt does not globally orient ko7System.

Given dimension d, arctic measure M over ko7Schema, certificate C, weight equality between C.weight and scalar weight, scalarization equality for all Trace terms, and unbounded scalarized range, M.eval with C.lt does not globally orient ko7System.

Given dimension d, tropical measure M over ko7Schema, certificate C, weight equality between C.weight and scalar weight, scalarization equality for all Trace terms, and unbounded scalarized range, M.eval with C.lt does not globally orient ko7System.
Given dimension d and functional measure M over ko7Schema with weight equal to row-sum weight and unbounded weighted range, M.eval with VecLt does not globally orient ko7System.
For any KO7 tropical measure and tracked coordinate, strict orientation of every full contextual KO7 step is impossible.
There exists a one-dimensional tropical measure with positive wrapper diagonals and a finite coordinate that strictly orients the root duplicating step for all b s n.

openPoints: Arctic-primary, tropical-primary, max and componentwise barriers require unbounded range or successor or wrapper pumps of at least one; below those thresholds the files draw no conclusion.

Certificate-backed arctic and tropical barriers require matching weight equality, scalarization equality for all terms, and unbounded scalarized range; without such certificates no barrier is claimed.
Natural nonincreasing orientation needs one positive coordinate value; the zero evaluation with unit wrapper diagonals shows positivity cannot be dropped.

Tropical root steps can be oriented by an explicit witness, but every tropical measure fails on the full wrapper-context closure; retaining at most one wrapper congruence restores orientability in the one-sided classification.

The Boolean row admits a monotone one-by-one interpretation that globally orients its system, so the blanket certificate-free lift barrier fails there; residual catalog rows record reduced, licensed-escape or split-closed statuses rather than proving orientation.

Residual taxonomy, lifts and reduction interfaces

files.summary: The file specializes the arctic primary-projection barrier to the KO7 schema and system. It proves that under an unbounded-range hypothesis on the projected max measure, there is no global ArcticLt orientation. The proof reduces a global orientation to a duplicating-step orientation and applies the general arctic barrier.
files.conclusion: Unbounded arctic primary range rules out global ArcticLt orientation of the KO7 system.

files.summary: The file defines the finite arctic carrier ArcticNat, the strict comparison ArcticLt on finite coordinates, and ArcticPrimaryMeasure embedding a MaxMeasure through the finite projection. It proves three obstructions transferring the max barrier to ArcticLt under unbounded-range, successor-pump, and wrap-pump hypotheses. Each proof converts an assumed ArcticLt orientation into a max strict inequality and applies the corresponding max result.
files.conclusion: Max-barrier obstructions transfer to ArcticLt under unbounded-range, successor-pump, and wrap-pump hypotheses.

files.summary: Specializes the tracked first-component dimension-2 barrier to KO7. Gives three theorems for unbounded first-component range, successor pump and wrap pump. Each reduces global Step orientation to the duplicating rec_succ step and applies the generic schema barrier.
files.conclusion: No tracked 2D componentwise measure orients all KO7 steps under the stated pumps.

files.summary: Defines dimension-2 componentwise affine measures where each coordinate is scalar affine, with projections and unbounded-range predicates. Proves first- and second-component affine failures each rule out componentwise pair orientation of the duplicating step. Gives successor-pump and wrap-pump corollaries and lifts the tracked barrier to global root orientation.
files.conclusion: Tracked-component affine failure rules out 2D componentwise orientation of the duplicating and global steps.

files.summary: Specializes the arbitrary mixed-matrix scalar-dominance barrier to KO7. Assuming an explicit weight, a dominance certificate linking the ambient order to scalarization, and unbounded scalarized range, no global orientation of the KO7 system exists.
files.conclusion: KO7 inherits the arbitrary-matrix scalar-dominance barrier.

files.summary: Defines unit and all-ones weights with scalarization lemmas. Proves fixed-row and equal-column-sum certificates for RespectsWeight. Derives fixed-row/unit and row-sum/all-ones instances of the arbitrary scalarization barrier for the duplicating step and wraps them to KO7 global orientation barriers.
files.conclusion: Fixed-row/unit and row-sum/all-ones scalarizations cannot orient the duplicating or global steps when unbounded.

files.summary: Defines finite natural vectors, scalarization, full mixed matrices with weight-respect laws, and arbitrary measures with explicit scalarization witnesses. Projects each such measure to a scalar affine measure. Proves that unboundedness plus scalar dominance of the ambient order rules out orientation of the duplicating step and global orientation.
files.conclusion: Explicitly scalarizable mixed-matrix measures cannot orient the duplicating or global steps under dominance and unboundedness.

files.summary: Lifts the certificate-free arctic barrier through system, KO7 and full one-hole context layers in nonincreasing, strict and pump-free strict forms. Exhibits a one-dimensional bot-right arctic interpretation that strictly orients the duplicating step, proving finiteness load-bearing. Gives a trace-weight size interpretation with positive wrapper diagonals that is blocked at both root and context layers.
files.conclusion: Arctic barriers lift to KO7 and full context, and the bot diagonal is a sharp escape.

files.summary: Develops arctic max-plus order, vectors, matrices and weight-free interpretations with positive versus finite diagonal predicates. Proves nonincreasing, strict and pump-free strict barriers by colliding wrapper-chain growth with a counter-matrix bound. Gives a finite-or-bot dichotomy and a constant fin-0 measure showing positivity is load-bearing for the nonincreasing form.
files.conclusion: Tracked arctic orientation is impossible under the stated diagonal and order premises, and the premises are sharp.

files.summary: Gives KO7 specializations of the certificate-backed arctic and tropical matrix barriers. Each assumes a comparison and scalarization certificate with matching weight and evaluation plus unbounded scalarized range. Each reduces global KO7 orientation to the duplicating step.
files.conclusion: KO7 inherits both certificate-backed arctic and tropical barriers.

files.summary: Defines fixed-row/unit and row-sum/all-ones comparisons for arctic and tropical carriers with reusable scalar-dominance certificates. Proves the four corresponding duplicating-step barriers under weight, scalarization and unboundedness hypotheses. Wraps each to a KO7 global orientation barrier.
files.conclusion: Unit and row-sum arctic/tropical barriers hold for the duplicating and KO7 global steps.

files.summary: Defines finite-vector arctic and tropical carriers, finite-part scalarizations, and explicit certificate and measure structures linking matrix evaluation to a scalar witness. Proves both certificate-backed barriers by reduction to projected primary dominance, conditional on supplied comparison and scalarization certificates.
files.conclusion: Certificate-backed arctic/tropical barriers reduce to the scalar dominance barrier.

files.summary: Specializes the tracked fixed-dimension componentwise barrier to KO7. Gives unbounded-tracked-range, successor-pump and wrap-pump versions for strict componentwise VecLt. Each forbids orientation of all Steps by reducing to the duplicating rec_succ step.
files.conclusion: KO7 inherits the tracked-dimension barrier in three pump forms.

files.summary: Defines strict componentwise order and fixed-dimension measures with tracked affine laws and wrapper positivity, with projection and unboundedness notions. Proves unbounded, succ-pump and wrap-pump barriers for the duplicating step and a global lift. Inhabits dimension two on free syntax with size tracked and counter depth untracked, discharging all premises while the untracked coordinate decreases yet pair orientation fails.
files.conclusion: Tracked-dimension componentwise orientation is impossible under the stated pumps, with a free-syntax witness showing the premises are satisfiable.

files.summary: Specializes the weighted componentwise functional matrix barrier to KO7. Gives unbounded-weighted-range, successor-pump and wrap-pump versions for strict componentwise VecLt. Each reduces global Step orientation to the duplicating rec_succ step.
files.conclusion: KO7 inherits the functional weighted-componentwise barrier.

files.summary: This file defines a finite-dimensional matrix-style measure through an explicit natural-weighted scalar projection with affine laws. It proves that strict componentwise decrease cannot orient the duplicating step when the weighted projection is unbounded or admits successor or wrapper pumps. It shows the tracked-coordinate and balanced mixed-coordinate families are instances of this functional barrier via singleton and all-ones weights.
files.conclusion: No weighted affine matrix measure with unbounded projection, or with a successor or wrapper pump, can strictly orient the duplicating step componentwise, and the tracked-coordinate and balanced mixed-coordinate families inherit this barrier.

files.summary: This file specializes the tracked primary-component lexicographic barrier to the KO7 kernel. It derives three KO7 global non-orientation results under PairLexLt from unbounded primary range, successor pump, and wrapper pump hypotheses. Each proof reduces global Step orientation to orientation of the duplicating step and applies the schema barrier.
files.conclusion: No tracked pair measure satisfying the stated pump or unboundedness hypothesis can globally orient KO7 steps in lexicographic order.

files.summary: This file specializes the finite-dimensional tracked-primary lexicographic barrier to KO7. It gives global KO7 non-orientation under VecLexLt from unbounded primary range, successor pump, and wrapper pump hypotheses. It also gives an unconditional KO7 specialization for the strengthened subclass carrying its own primary pump.
files.conclusion: No finite tracked-primary lexicographic measure satisfying the stated pump or unboundedness hypothesis can globally orient KO7 steps.

files.summary: This module generalizes the tracked-primary lexicographic barrier from dimension 2 to arbitrary fixed finite dimension. It defines the primary index and lexicographic order, shows lexicographic decrease forces primary nonincrease, and projects the primary coordinate to the scalar affine barrier. It proves unbounded-primary, successor-pump, wrapper-pump, strengthened internal-pump, and global no-orientation theorems.
files.conclusion: No finite tracked-primary lexicographic measure with unbounded or pumped primary coordinate can orient the duplicating step, hence no such system is globally oriented lexicographically.

files.summary: This file gives the KO7 specialization of the strengthened permutation-priority lexicographic barrier. It states that any finite-dimensional measure with an internal primary pump cannot globally orient KO7 under its permuted lexicographic order. The proof is direct application of the schema global theorem.
files.conclusion: Every permutation-priority lexicographic measure with an internal primary pump fails to globally orient KO7.

files.summary: This module proves conditional barriers for lexicographic vector orders after a supplied coordinate permutation. It defines the permuted primary index and permuted lexicographic order and shows such decrease forces permuted-primary nonincrease. It projects that coordinate to the affine barrier and derives unbounded-primary, successor-pump, wrapper-pump, strengthened internal-pump, and global theorems.
files.conclusion: No permutation-priority lexicographic measure with unbounded or pumped permuted-primary coordinate can orient the duplicating step, hence none globally orients its system.

files.summary: This module extends the tracked-component pair barrier from strict componentwise to lexicographic order with tracked primary scope. It defines PairLexLt and shows lexicographic decrease forces first-component nonincrease. It proves that a pumpable strict primary increase blocks lexicographic orientation and derives successor-pump, wrapper-pump, and global corollaries.
files.conclusion: No tracked pair lexicographic measure with unbounded or pumped primary coordinate can orient the duplicating step, hence none globally orients its system.

files.summary: This file specializes the balanced mixed-coordinate dimension-2 barrier to KO7. It states that a MatrixMix2Measure with unbounded coordinate-sum range cannot globally orient KO7 under PairLt. The proof applies the schema global theorem directly.
files.conclusion: No balanced mixed-coordinate measure with unbounded coordinate sum can globally orient KO7 under strict pair order.

files.summary: This module proves a conditional barrier for a balanced two-coordinate mixed projection. It defines coordinate sums, balanced 2x2 maps, and a mixed affine measure whose sum projection is affine. It shows strict pair decrease forces strict sum decrease and derives sum-pump duplicating-step and global no-orientation theorems from the scalar affine barrier.
files.conclusion: No balanced mixed-coordinate measure with unbounded coordinate sum can orient the duplicating step under strict pair order, hence none globally orients its system.

files.summary: This module instantiates the certificate-free natural-matrix barrier at KO7 for strict tracked, nonincreasing, componentwise, EWZ, and lexicographic orders. It proves a unit-weight certificate implies wrapper-diagonal positivity, hence the certificate-free barrier applies. It supplies a one-dimensional size witness and a two-dimensional mixed witness whose wrapper matrices share no nonzero weight, separating the certificate-free barrier from all certificate-backed barriers.
files.conclusion: Positive wrapper diagonals block all tracked strict and, with one positive value, nonincreasing orders without certificates or pumps, and the mixed witness separates this barrier from every certificate-backed barrier.

files.summary: This file shows EWZ strict monotonicity forces positive wrapper diagonals, so the certificate-free natural-matrix barrier applies with no extra premise. It proves duplicating-step and global failures under EWZ, componentwise, and positive lexicographic orders. It compiles the zero-diagonal interpretation as a non-example where nonstrict comparison holds but EWZ monotonicity and diagonal positivity fail.
files.conclusion: Every EWZ-monotone natural matrix interpretation fails the duplicating step under EWZ, componentwise and positive lexicographic orders, and the zero interpretation shows the diagonal hypothesis cannot be dropped.

files.summary: This schema proves a certificate-free, dimension-uniform natural-matrix barrier over Nat. It defines NatMatrixMeasure and wrapper-diagonal positivity and shows the wrapper dominates argument coordinates. It proves unconditional failure for orders forcing strict tracked decrease and conditional failure with one positive value for merely nonincreasing orders. It instantiates componentwise, EWZ, lexicographic, priority, Pareto, cone, and norm orders and their global forms.
files.conclusion: Positive wrapper diagonals alone rule out all tracked-strict orders and, with one positive value, all tracked-nonincreasing orders without certificates or pumps.

files.summary: This schema lifts the natural-matrix barrier to nonnegative elements of ordered semirings. It defines field vectors, matrices and measures with nonnegativity, proves wrapper lower bounds, boundedness under nonincrease, strict boundedness with cancellation, doubling along wrapper chains, and Archimedean unboundedness. It gives unbounded, Archimedean positive, and unconditional strict barriers, shows positivity is necessary via a zero evaluation with unit diagonals, and coerces Nat measures to NNRat and NNReal.
files.conclusion: Positive wrapper diagonals block strict tracked matrix orientation over ordered semirings unconditionally and block nonincreasing orientation under Archimedean positivity, with NNRat and NNReal instances by coercion.

files.summary: This file proves a tropical context obstruction for min-plus matrix interpretations. It defines the wrapper-context closure, canonical chains and stages, and finite tropical caps, then shows a strict right step forces a finite right contribution that bounds all left contributions against arbitrarily long recursor runs. It derives universal, finite-bias, and finite-cap no-go theorems, transfers them to free syntax and full KO7 contexts, exhibits the root-versus-context split, and classifies which wrapper-congruence policies remain orientable by one-sided measures.
files.conclusion: No tropical matrix interpretation strictly orients the wrapper-context closure, while root orientation exists and one-sided wrapper policies are exactly those that remain orientable.

files.summary: This file defines the tropical natural semiring, vectors, matrices and their min-plus action, plus tropical matrix interpretations of step-duplicating schemas. It proves the diagonal entry is an upper bound for the action, reversing the lower-bound pump used over natural and arctic semirings. It compiles an explicit one-dimensional witness with positive wrapper diagonals that strictly orients the root duplicating step, killing the certificate-free tropical barrier, and shows the witness lacks scalar dominance and fails wrapper-context compatibility.
files.conclusion: The certificate-free tropical matrix barrier is false via an explicit one-dimensional orienting witness that does not extend to wrapper contexts.

files.summary: This file defines theorem-visible interfaces for componentwise weak-strict, Pareto, lex-priority, permutation lex-priority, scalarizable and import-dependent matrix orders. It proves projection payloads saying each weak-monotone family scalarizes for every weight and the scalarizable family carries its own dominance certificate. It also records that import-dependent matrices are licensed escapes and the unconstrained relation is not yet a method class.
files.conclusion: Each weak-monotone matrix order family scalarizes and the licensed and unconstrained rows carry their catalog statuses.

files.summary: This file introduces matrix-over-polynomial relations as payload exposure matrices with an abstract cross-coupling proposition slot. It proves the canonical observer cannot globally orient the family when the distinguished payload coordinate has an unbounded pump. It packages this non-orientation with the projection identity as a correspondence certificate.
files.conclusion: Every matrix-over-polynomial with a payload pump fails to globally orient its family, with an explicit correspondence certificate.

files.summary: This file gives two KO7-facing corollaries of the matrix projection barriers. A fixed tracked row with an unbounded componentwise pump cannot globally orient KO7 steps. The all-ones row-sum weighting gives the same conclusion as a concrete weighted-functional instance.
files.conclusion: Unbounded fixed-row and row-sum matrix interpretations cannot globally orient KO7 steps.

files.summary: This file specializes imported matrix barriers to two projection patterns. It defines the all-ones row-sum weight and proves fixed-row corollaries under unbounded, successor-pump and row-sum hypotheses. Each corollary says the corresponding pumped matrix interpretation cannot orient the duplicating step.
files.conclusion: Fixed-row and row-sum pumps each block uniform orientation of the duplicating step.

files.summary: This file builds a ten-row theorem-backed catalog of residual matrix closures. It assigns families, statuses, support kinds and support propositions to each row, with reduction, licensed-escape and unrestricted-split closures. It proves every row has inhabited support and the finite final-catalog predicate holds exactly.
files.conclusion: All ten catalog rows carry theorem-backed support and the finite catalog predicate holds exactly.

files.summary: This file defines the exact finite taxonomy of residual matrix families and engine-grade closure labels. It gives the ten-family inventory and the status function sending reduction families to reduced, arctic and tropical to licensed escape, legacy unconstrained to not-yet and closed unconstrained to split-closed. It proves inventory completeness and the status catalog.
files.conclusion: The ten residual families carry their exact closure statuses with the unconstrained-closed family promoted to split-closed.

files.summary: This file packages six reviewer-facing fixed-row and row-sum search fragments for arbitrary, arctic and tropical matrices. Each fragment carries weight and scalarize identities plus unbounded range, and each is proved to admit no global orientation. The blocked layer is shown to refine the scalarizable, arctic-full and tropical-full residual statuses.
files.conclusion: All six fixed-row and row-sum fragments are blocked and refine the exact residual statuses at scalarizable, arctic and tropical rows.

files.summary: This file connects the acyclic six-kind split core to the residual catalog. It proves both compatibility rows carry split-closed status and named-theorem support backed by the six-kind length and final catalog. It also defines an audit anchor string for the unconditional theorem.
files.conclusion: Both unconstrained catalog rows carry split-closed status and support backed by the six-kind theorem.

files.summary: This acyclic core splits the unconstrained matrix surface into six certificate kinds with structural carriers for row-column, cone, norm and non-scalarizable orders. It proves per-kind unconditional payloads by scalarization or licensed arctic and tropical barriers, plus unique classification of every relation. The headline bundles exact six-kind enumeration, per-kind closure and unique classification.
files.conclusion: Every matrix relation classifies uniquely into six unconditionally closed certificate kinds.

files.summary: This file specializes the schema max barrier to KO7. An unbounded max range blocks global root orientation, and positive successor drift or wrap drift each supply such a pump. All three KO7 specializations forbid global orientation by max measures.
files.conclusion: Unbounded and pumped max measures cannot globally orient KO7.

files.summary: This file promotes the max-depth obstruction to a schema-level max-plus family with fixed unary and wrapper bumps. Positive successor or wrap drift pumps the family to unbounded range. Once the pumped step dominates frozen branches, the wrapper carries it visibly, so no max measure orients the duplicating step or its global form.
files.conclusion: Unbounded and pumped max-plus measures cannot orient the duplicating step or its global root form.

files.summary: This file specializes the bounded multilinear barrier to KO7 root orientation. Unbounded range with base-point dominance blocks global orientation. Positive successor drift or wrap drift each supply the needed pump under the same dominance hypothesis.
files.conclusion: Pumped bounded-multilinear measures satisfying base dominance cannot globally orient KO7.

files.summary: This file extends the scalar barrier to finite multilinear recursors where each variable occurs at most once per monomial. After freezing base, the table becomes affine in the pumped step with a frozen coefficient sum. If wrapper gain dominates that coefficient at the base, unbounded, successor-pumped or wrap-pumped measures cannot orient the duplicating step or its global form.
files.conclusion: Dominated bounded-multilinear measures with unbounded or pumped range cannot orient the duplicating step.

files.summary: Records a closed seven-row tag-level universe of named ordered-semiring bases and their matrix-algebra targets. Defines the total lift function, the uniform preservesMonotonicity tag, and the exhaustive enumerations. Proves the unconditional five-part conjunction of totality, exhaustiveness, image structure, universal monotonicity status and non-vacuity by decide and rfl.
files.conclusion: Over the closed seven-row universe every named base semiring lifts to a matrix algebra with monotone status, exhaustively and non-vacuously.

files.summary: Packages a uniform tag-keyed barrier certificate with affine Nat-valued scalarization, order-respect and unboundedness. Proves unconditionally that no such certificate-backed monotone matrix interpretation over any base-semiring lift orients the duplicating step, with a global-system version. Discharges the arctic, tropical and natural rows explicitly from existing matrix measures and dominance shims.
files.conclusion: No certificate-backed monotone matrix interpretation over any of the seven lifted algebras orients the duplicating step, discharged explicitly for arctic, tropical and natural rows.

files.summary: Isolates the theorem-backed subclass of natural, arctic and tropical rows and characterizes it exactly. Constructs a concrete monotone 1x1 Boolean interpretation on a two-point schema whose induced system globally orients the duplicating step. Packages this as a boundary theorem showing the certificate-free blanket barrier fails on the Boolean row.
files.conclusion: The unconditional certificate-free matrix-lift barrier is false because the Boolean row admits an explicit monotone globally orienting interpretation.

files.summary: This file specializes the tropical primary-projection barrier to the KO7 schema and system. It proves that no tropical primary measure with unbounded projected max globally orients KO7.
files.conclusion: No tropical primary measure with unbounded projected max globally orients the KO7 system.

files.summary: This file defines tropical primary measures as eval with a Nat primary projection identified with a max measure. It proves three schema-generic barriers showing no such measure orients the duplicating step under unbounded, successor-pump, or wrap-pump hypotheses. Each proof reduces strict lt orientation to a max-measure inequality already ruled out.
files.conclusion: No tropical primary measure orients the duplicating schema step under any of the three stated max-pump conditions.

files.summary: This file checks MatrixBarrierArbitrary instances. It elaborates unit and all-ones weights, fixed-row and column-sum respect lemmas, local no-orientation theorems for unit and row-sum pumps and the corresponding global no-orientation theorems. It proves no new content.
files.conclusion: Unit and row-sum scalar-dominance pumps block any global matrix-arbitrary orientation.

files.summary: This file instantiates the arbitrary-matrix barrier with a concrete one-dimensional measure. It defines constant vectors, an all-ones matrix, a simple-size matrix measure, a scalar order and dominance, proves unbounded scalarized range, and exhibits local and global non-orientation examples. It checks the abstract barrier theorems by instantiation.
files.conclusion: The simple-size matrix measure with an unbounded pump witnesses that no scalar-dominance order globally orients the duplicating step.

files.summary: This file instantiates arctic and tropical matrix barriers with one- and two-dimensional measures. It defines scalar vectors, unit and diagonal matrices, arctic-unit and tropical row-sum measures with scalarization lemmas and unboundedness proofs, and exhibits local arctic and global tropical non-orientation examples. It also checks the abstract arctic and tropical certificates and no-go theorems.
files.conclusion: Concrete arctic and tropical measures witness that no unit or row-sum interpretation orients the duplicating step globally.

files.summary: This file is a reach check for MatrixBarrierArcticTropical. It checks arctic and tropical vectors, finite parts, certificates and measures, plus local and global no-orientation theorems for scalar-dominance pumps. It proves no new content.
files.conclusion: No arctic or tropical matrix measure orients the duplicating step or the system globally.

files.summary: This file is a permanent reach and axiom gate for tropical context-closure no-go results. It checks tropical contexts, wrap chains, canonical stages, transitivity and evaluation bounds, uniform-cap and finite-bias impossibility, free and KO7 transfers, escape-measure universality, root classification and the wrapper-policy classification with positive and negative witnesses. It proves no new theorems.
files.conclusion: Uniform finite tropical caps universally forbid orientation, with only the one-sided policy orienting.

files.summary: The file defines a tracked index in Fin 1 and six one-dimensional matrix-order instances covering componentwise, Pareto, lexicographic, permutation-lexicographic, scalarizable and import-dependent interfaces. It runs #check directives for the interface types and their projection and closure-status lemmas. It then checks strict-coordinate, scalar-dominance, tracked-primary, projection-payload and licensed-escape or not-yet-method-class claims on those instances.
files.conclusion: The six one-coordinate orders type-check as instances and satisfy their strict-coordinate, dominance, primary-tracked, projection and closure-status checks.

files.summary: This file is a reach check for the matrix residual closure catalog. It checks catalog rows, families, statuses, nodup and length, exact completeness, taxonomy matching, honest statuses, support kinds and supports, and the final catalog and certificate projections. Seven examples verify membership, statuses and supports.
files.conclusion: The catalog is exact with support for every row including legacy and arctic escapes.

files.summary: This file is a reach and axiom check for the matrix residual taxonomy. It checks families, closure statuses, inventories, nodup, length, exact completeness and the status catalog with axiom prints. Five examples verify membership, reduced versus open statuses and the completeness equivalence.
files.conclusion: The residual inventory is exact with scalarizable weight reduced and unconstrained relation still open.

files.summary: This file is a reach check for matrix tool-search mapping. It checks fixed-row, row-sum, arctic and tropical fragments, their fragment-level no-global-orientation theorems, the residual-status hook type and the refinement theorem. One example inhabits the hook from the refinement theorem.
files.conclusion: Projection fragments refine exactly the residual statuses while admitting no global orientation.

files.summary: This file is a reach test for MatrixUnrestrictedSplit. It checks the six-kind enum, nodup and length, completeness, per-kind payloads and unconditional closure, the classification and final-catalog theorems and the anchor string. Twelve examples verify membership, closure, catalog projections and the anchor.
files.conclusion: All six matrix certificate kinds are unconditionally closed with a unique-kind final catalog.

files.summary: This file imports the abstract ordered-semiring matrix-lift barrier module and checks ten public declarations for the Boolean one-dimensional lift. It contains six examples showing the arctic and tropical semirings satisfy the lift barrier predicate, the Boolean semiring lifts to the Boolean matrix tag yet fails the predicate, and a monotone Boolean matrix schema both has an orienting instance and refutes a uniform certificate-free barrier. The examples are derived from the boundary theorem and the certificate-free barrier statement.
files.conclusion: The strongest checked claim is that the arctic and tropical semirings admit the lift barrier while the boolean semiring does not, although some monotone Boolean instance does orient.

files.summary: This file imports the ordered-semiring matrix-lift barrier module and checks the lift-barrier certificate API with its arbitrary, arctic, tropical and natural unconditional theorems. It contains four examples that instantiate the arbitrary, arctic, tropical and natural barrier statements to show no certificate or measure with unbounded scalarized range orients all wrap-versus-recur steps. The examples carry the required weight, scalarize and unbounded-range hypotheses.
files.conclusion: The strongest checked claim is the unconditional barrier that no matrix-lift certificate with unbounded range orients all duplicating steps.

files.summary: This file imports the ordered-semiring matrix-lift module and checks base and matrix kinds, the lift map, monotonicity status, list completeness and the unconditional universe theorem with its audit anchor. It contains seven examples that destructure the universe theorem and evaluate concrete tags, list length and the audit anchor string. The file proves no new theory beyond these elaboration checks.
files.conclusion: The file verifies that the seven-element base universe lifts completely with preserved monotonicity.

files.summary: This file confirms reachability of the Phase C vector, matrix and tuple lift on a concrete carrier. It defines a single-payload single-position Bool family with payload count rising from 1 to 2 and checks projection identity. It exhibits the canonical exposure matrix, its DWO lift, matrix-over-polynomial non-orientability and correspondence, tuple row trichotomy, and the phase-C capstone on that carrier.
files.conclusion: The concrete Bool/Unit family witnesses projection identity, matrix-over-polynomial non-orientability, correspondence, row trichotomy, and phase-C closure.
